· Cause of death: fracture to the back of the skull (occipital) and brain haemorrhage.
· The shape of the fracture is not consistent with striking a straight edge; it is consistent with a blow from a round, hard object or one backed by a fist. No kerb line.
· A fresh punch mark on the left cheekbone; before the fall.
· Grazes on the fingers of the right hand; as if gripping something tightly.
· Blood alcohol 0.9 per mille.
· Wallet and keys found on him. No phone.

Gareth Hollis, Paul Ainsworth and Steve Barker were tried for perverting the course of justice. Frank Doyle’s licence was revoked. The last line of the fax: “A separate inquiry has been opened into the district liaison chief who signed the handover letter.”
The defence presented it as ‘honest error’; no action was taken against the three witnesses.
The four officers testified at Garrett’s trial that ‘we may have been mistaken’; Garrett was acquitted.
Why the statements matched stayed open in the file; the three witnesses returned to duty.
Frank Doyle was taken into custody and confessed to the bribes; no link to the death could be made, and he was released. His statement alone was not enough against Garrett.
Neil Garrett was arrested for manslaughter and bribery. Divers found Callum’s phone in the river by a wharf near Garrett’s home; the SIM card was read.
The death was closed as an accident. The four witnesses signed off the file; Callum’s cloud backup was never opened.
Ryan Webb was arrested. Four police officers testified; the young man got six years. Neil Garrett was promoted to inspector the following year.

Frank sold Callum out; that is on his conscience. But that night he was in the kitchen, and he was not the one who went outside.

Only his colleagues said Garrett was in the smoking area; the barmaid saw him leave by the front door after Callum, and the taxi camera recorded someone pulling Callum by the arm at 23.12. Callum had filmed Garrett taking bribes, and Frank had told him.
The autopsy shows a blow inconsistent with the kerb and a punch mark from before the fall. The phone is missing; last sync 23.12.
Ryan left by the back door at 23.05; his card was read two streets away at 23.09. Steve Barker, who gave his name to 999, didn’t know him; someone whispered the name in his ear.

SCENE PLAN — THE LAMPLIGHTER AND TANNER LANE

On 13 April 2029 at 23.16, 999 was told that a man was lying injured on the pavement outside The Lamplighter pub, Tanner Lane, Bermondsey. Callum Reid (33) died at the scene.

Witness statement (to the area patrol, 23.40): “One of two men who’d scuffled inside at closing, a young builder called Ryan, pushed Callum again outside. Callum fell backwards, hit his head on the corner of the kerb. We were in the smoking area, all four of us saw it.”

Statement given, and report written the next morning, by: Paul Ainsworth. The file was transferred to bube London as a routine suspicious death.

Witness and 999 caller.
What I saw. I asked for an ambulance.

In front of the smoking area, on the pavement. I was looking at my phone, heard the noise and looked up.

On the 999 recording.
…Neil told me. He’d heard the name when they fought inside. While I was calling he kept saying in my ear, ‘Say Ryan, Ryan.’
He turned his phone face down on the table.
On the call you said ‘the one who pushed him is called Ryan’. How did you know that lad by name?
I don’t know. I really don’t. Neil had two phones in his hand, that’s all.

The scene plan showed that the side wall and the van cut the line of sight of witnesses who said ‘we saw it from the smoking area’. The bar terminal put one witness inside at that minute, and the card record put Ryan two streets away. The staff record revealed the witnesses were colleagues, the taxi camera and the barmaid that Garrett went out after Callum, and the cloud backup the reason.
Before asking what a witness saw, ask where they could see from. Four statements that agree are not four pieces of evidence; four mouths saying the same sentence are a single source.
Bermondsey, Tanner Lane — 12–14 April 2029

Callum Reid filmed the envelope that pub owner Frank Doyle gave Deputy Inspector Neil Garrett every month, and was preparing to send it to a journalist. Frank told Garrett. At closing time Garrett went out after Callum, demanded the phone, punched Callum when he resisted and struck his head; he took the fallen man’s phone and went back to the smoking area. Three off-duty officers from the same unit joined a single story blaming Ryan Webb, who had scuffled inside; one of the witnesses wrote the report.
Who is responsible for Callum Reid’s death?
